thread.title: Enphase Energy's Latest Victories - Enphase Energy Inc. (NASDAQ:ENPH)

author: TJ Roberts
title: Enphase Energy's Latest Victories - Enphase Energy Inc. (NASDAQ:ENPH)

organizations.name: enphase energy's latest victories - enphase energy inc.

text:
With the recent SunPower deal , Enphase Energy ( ENPH ) is victorious in the microinverter arena. Clearly, Enphase management is taking care of the business, and has now forged a powerful partnership and an alliance for the future. As CEO Kothandaraman said at the conference , it’s “ in both parties best interest to get ” the business relationship running smoothly as quickly as possible which adds crucial ingredients “ incentive ” and “ synergy ” to the new relationship. Faster installation, easier to install, simpler solution, increased productivity, safer, longer-lasting and better performance are key reasons Enphase is gaining traction with installers. With this deal, the standardization of MLPE using Enphase Energized microinverters comes even closer to reality. Read on to gain more perspective and see why Enphase, in my opinion, is the Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) of solar.
With the acquisition of SunPower’s ( SPWR ) SolarBridge , the last major competitor for Enphase’s dominance of the microinverter arena has been removed, save for a few stragglers. APS and Hoymiles are out there, and even LG isn't yet firmly entrenched with Enphase Energized since they’re still selling their own microinverter, as well as the Enphase-integrated NeON-2 ACe . Regardless of these, Kothandaraman made it very clear at the conference that Enphase is a “ 10-year-cycle of learning,” meaning, it’s difficult if not too late for newcomers, for Enphase's technology is far too advanced; Enphase’s microinverters are software driven by an ASIC that’s taken over a decade to mature and cannot be easily reverse-engineered.
With SunPower’s microinverter business, Enphase will gain access to 13 of the top 16 homebuilders in California, besides the ones they already have, and then there’s the 2020 mandate just around the corner; in addition to these facts, the recent SunPower-Sonnen partnership offered verifiable proof of new vertical markets opening up for Enphase; in the article, Enphase should have been mentioned, but that was okay, for the article presented a viable solution to Enphase’s large storage need; ACBs can remain a low-end storage solution, while SunPower-Enphase-Sonnen can take the high-end. The PV-magazine article beautifully stated that “ collaboration provides best-in-class sustainable technology solutions for the growing number of households seeking high-performance products that support a future for clean energy; ” so, if SolarEdge ( SEDG ) collaborated with SolarCity growing MLPE marketshare from 4% to 40% in just 2 years, then surely Enphase collaborating with these giants has that same potential. With Enphase’s recent entry into the German market, having this partnership synergy can only complement the effort. Furthermore, consider the hundreds of SunPower dealers out there, and a recent statement by one Florida dealer provides a microcosm of the synergy brewing - “ we’ve had great results with IQ6, and we’re coming back to Enphase, ” said Damon Egglefield, president of Mirasol Solar in Sarasota . With these types of partnerships being fomented, Enphase may never even need to set foot in some of these markets, for their partners will do it for them.
Looking at Google trends ( below ), the SunPower deal adds 29 new regions for Enphase, and strengthens Enphase's existing 21 regions. Most SunPower regions are likely utility, but ACMs could have LCOE advantage in some C/I as panel wattages increase.
Recall that SunPower’s acquisition of SolarBridge in 2014 resulted in the Equinox , a product that went from 67 % (p.5) , 80% ( p.6 ), 85 % ( p.4 ), to 90% ( p.4 ) of the company’s residential product portfolio in just a year. Both Enphase and SunPower see ACMs as the future of solar on the rooftop, and now they are united. The “ synergy ” mentioned by Kothandaraman in the last earnings call is now happening. Surely, SunPower recognized the microinverter revenue loss of SolarBridge, but now their ACMs will have IQ and inherit all of the advances without having to spend hundreds of millions in R&D money to catch up with Enphase - polymer casing, fan-less inverters, 2-wire config, tree-structured topology, detachable micro, et cetera. Now, ACMs will be united across partner product portfolios because they’ll all be Enphase Energized - SunPower, Solaria , Panasonic ( OTCPK:PCRFY ), LG ( OTC:LGEAF ), JinkoSolar ( JKS ), Waaree, with likely more partners coming. At the conference, it was asked how Enphase partners would view the deal, and Kothandaraman gave an excellent reply stating Enphase is “ here to make all our module partners successful. ” Soon, solar panel companies without an AC Module may be viewed as behind the times, and Enphase will become the standard, integrated MLPE. The fact that a string inverter solution is “ one box too many " in the vertical market world, as well as a warranty liability, ( see SEDG warranty use/settlement trend graph below ) is going to be to Enphase’s advantage in the long run.
One interesting reason the SunPower-SolarBridge acquisition was such a surprise is that in October 2014, Enphase had sued SolarBridge for patent infringement . SunPower, backed by Total S.A., had swooped in a month later and acquired SolarBridge; this led to an unexpected, early case dismissal in April 2015, which truly closed the door connecting Enphase and SunPower, making them arch rivals. Therefore, it is safe to say that with Enphase’s previous management, the SunPower deal would never have happened, but with SunPower hero and Enphase director, TJ Rodgers, and the men who have worked with him and are now leading the 2 companies involved - CEOs Badri Kothandaraman and Tom Werner - that chemistry alone surely made the deal possible.
The SunPower-Enphase deal is going to push the limits of Enphase’s budgetary 30-20-10 ( p.13 ) to 33-21-12. Consider it an immense " gift " from SunPower, but don’t forget SunPower inherited a 10-year cycle of product R&D worth over $100M. Likely, the two partners will now plan a 30-40% ACM sales expansion abroad, so this $70M deal can actually be viewed as ~$100M once the overseas business kicks in. If we assume $80M/qtr or $320M/yr, then along with $65M SolarBridge revenue, that’s ~$385M annual. Taking 4 quarters of OpEx at $20.25M gives ~21%, and operating income would be ~12%; so a 33/21/12 target operating model could be achieved.
They say the devil is in the details ( table below ), and if you compare warranty expenses for the MLPE market contenders, Enphase and SolarEdge, you can see that 1) Enphase management has seriously optimized service with revolutionary products like IQ7PD , which will allow all legacy warranty replacements to be fulfilled by an IQ7 product at a much lower cost, but 2) for SolarEdge, hefty warranty expenses seem to be growing faster than sales. Enphase is now leagues better than SolarEdge in this realm with ~$6M/y on 17M microinverters in the field versus SolarEdge’s ~$16M/y on 22M optimizers and 1M inverters.
In 2019, Enphase should receive additional revenue of ~$70M at an impressive budgetary projection of 35/6/21 (p.8) . With IQ8 microgrid on track for Q4 and with the partner alliance, Enphase can recoup lost marketshare. According to NREL’s latest Solar Industry Update , Enphase and SolarEdge hold 66% of the residential solar inverter market, and with the latest acquisition pegging marketshare for Enphase at ~27% and SunPower at 9%, that practically puts the MLPE contenders in a dead heat.
Consider that if SolarEdge share price is at ~$50 with ~45M shares outstanding, then Enphase should be at about $12/share with its ~96M shares outstanding and half the revenue. The 4 main “ levers ” to make that happen were provided by Kothandaraman at the last earnings call where Enphase can grow SAM and marketshare with IQ, and even get back into C/I in cases where AC-coupled microinverters can achieve LCOE over string.
Regional expansion with IQ7 worldwide SKU ( 1GW SAM ) IQ7X addressing 96-cell market ( 500MW SAM ) Existing ACM partners and possibly new ones ( new housing, housing association, ESCo's ) IQ8 Ensemble - upgrade opportunity for 760k+ installed-based and complete new SAM growth target from 4GW to 10GW with 2.5x revenue growth In summary, hold onto your shares, for the Enphase train is picking up speed. Enphase has just crossed the Rubicon , and MLPE dominance in residential solar is on the horizon. At the last conference, Kothandaraman stressed that the health of the company, even without the SunPower deal, is fine, and from recent SP performance, analysts and institutions are coming to that realization, too.
 ENPH.
Additional disclosure: I have been intricately involved in the solar industry since 2010 after being introduced to Enphase's microinverter solar technology at SEIA in Paonia, Colorado. With 85 Enphase microinverters on my home, I have not incurred a real utility bill since 2013. I live in the Sunshine State where you would expect solar to be more prominent than it currently is, but times are changing, and people are starting to realize that solar isn't as expensive as it once was, and the technology is much more efficient than it was 10 years ago. Thanks for reading the article. Cheers!
